diagnosis.summary: Leak at the J-bend slip joint, most likely a worn or misaligned slip washer.

safety: Put a bucket under the trap before loosening the nuts.
Hand-tighten plastic slip nuts; pliers can crack them.
tools: channel-lock pliers (optional, for a stuck nut only)

steps.text: Put a bucket under the trap and hand-loosen slip nut [[part:p3]] counter-clockwise.
Slide the nut up and pull out the old washer [[part:p4]].
Fit the new 1-1/2 in washer with its flat side against the nut and its tapered side toward the fitting.
Seat the J-bend, hand-tighten the nut, run water for a minute and check for drips.

bom.name: 1-1/2 in slip-joint washer
bom.spec: polyethylene, beveled, fits 1-1/2 in tubular drain

followups: Want me to show you which way the bevel faces?
